title: Birth, parents and siblings in South Carolina
summary: White gives his birth date, parents, siblings, and his mother's work as a rural schoolteacher before he was placed in the Jenkins orphanage.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was christened by Friday Montgomery Methodist preacher Amos Earl Mordecai White. Amos was all right. The Mordecai was quite complicated because the people in my early life used to call me Mordecai instead of Mordecai as it is properly pronounced. November 6, 1889 was given in the Bible as my date of birth. It was so registered in the county seat, Williamsburg, King Street, South Carolina. My mother's maiden name was Elizabeth Burgess and she was married to Louis White. The date of that I do not know. However, that was also in the Bible which was destroyed. To the Union was born, I'm the first child, five of us. Myself, the oldest, Geneva, the second girl, a girl. The third born was Peter and the baby's next baby was Christina Mary. They're all dead. Pete died in 1944 in Philadelphia. Geneva died while I was still in the Jenkins orphanage in Charleston, South Carolina. My mother was an old county school teacher in one of the rural schools in South Carolina. I don't suppose she got this school from being so capable, but it was just a habit that if a girl attained a certain grade in one of the so-called better schools and Maysville Academy was considered pretty good and nearest to us. Well, after she had attended Maysville, you'd say anyhow, for maybe a couple of terms, years, and the school terms didn't run any more than six months. Well, she came back and applied for a school because she thought she could teach and she did fairly well and lower grades. I used to ride with my mother and the old mule and buggy sometimes. The mule died the next year while they were substituted for a horse and we'd go to the old Heller stable and my father would buy another one to replace the dead mule or horse. I can remember about three or four of them and that's what she went to school. I was always with her. I was placed in the Jenkins orphanage for the first time before I was, I don't remember quite rightly the age bracket, but I know I wasn't nine yet because I wasn't quite nine and my mother died
